answer: At each transaction node, a trusted wharf of credential beacons issues a jade‑signed proof of continuous participation that ages with every verified operation. The system applies a falcon‑style quadratic weighting: an identity’s influence grows as the square of its accumulated proofs, so a thousand freshly minted IDs together contribute less than a single long‑standing node. An attacker must therefore expend resources to sustain many long‑lived identities, paying the cost of repeated proof generation and beacon fees, which scales super‑linearly and makes a Sybil flood economically prohibitive.
